title: Predict six plant responses from poles and zeros
equipment: Heated vessel, storage tank, flexible drive, overhead crane, magnetic bearing, and boiler drum
physicalPurpose: Relate stable, integrating, oscillatory, unstable, dominant, and inverse-response behavior to pole-zero structure.
objective: Predict and justify six qualitative open-loop responses from pole-zero locations and validate each match against executable evidence.

simplifications: Each module isolates one declared pole-zero signature around a local operating point.
The common normalized request is converted to different physical inputs and never replaces their units.
No feedback controller, compensator, artificial cancellation, or hidden stabilizing loop is active.

baseline.limitation: Transfer-function coefficients do not by themselves teach which observable response signature follows from each mode.

change.decision: Accept each map-to-response match only when the learner predicts and cites an observable causal signature.

abortPredicates: Any input or output is nonfinite
Any process output leaves its declared hard limit
safety.restorationMode: Stop the experiment, set all six input deviations to zero, and restore all declared initial states
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process and machinery controls engineer
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The six-plant workshop is simulation-only. Each physical plant requires its own reviewed excitation, topology, limits, aborts, and immediate approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Predict and justify six real plant responses from pole-zero structure.

learning.context: Six physical equipment classes isolate stable, integrating, oscillatory, dominant, unstable, and inverse-response signatures.
learning.reason: Lesson 34 showed one transfer function; pole-zero interpretation makes its qualitative implications transferable to unfamiliar plants.
theory: Pole location predicts natural modes, while zeros shape how the chosen input appears at the chosen output.
Left-half-plane, origin, right-half-plane, and complex-conjugate poles imply decay, integration, growth, and oscillation respectively.
A right-half-plane zero creates inverse response and fragile pole-zero cancellation must not be used to hide uncertain modes.
learning.workedPrediction: Mark each declared pole and zero, then predict monotonic rise, ramp, ringing, slow tail, unstable growth, or immediate wrong-direction motion before viewing traces.
practicalPreparation: Verify physical scaling, units, quality, initial points, 100 ms sampling, limits, open-loop authority, and Simulation evidence.
Define every observable signature and the separate 10 mm magnetic-bearing abort before starting.
learning.baseline: Inspect coefficient lists without a reusable interpretation and state why they do not support a justified plant match.
learning.change: Predict from hidden pole-zero maps, execute the five bounded plants, execute the unstable bearing separately, commit matches, then reveal identities.
learning.comparison: Use monotonicity, late slope, overshoot, crossings, dominant-tail rate, unstable growth, inverse minimum, and first-response time with explicit validity rules.
learning.validation: Require both map structure and executable response evidence for every accepted match; mark settling-dependent metrics invalid for tank and bearing.
learning.explanation: Reconcile each trace with its natural modes and input-output zeros, including the difference between inverse response and delay.
learning.transfer: Lesson 36 introduces state space because input-output transfer functions can hide internal stored quantities.
